messages:
netbot: ALERT: intermittent 1-3% packet loss observed on geneve overlay in us-west-2 (nodepool-gpu). Pattern: sawtooth losses ~20-40s intervals. Affected pods: gpu-training-*/0-3.

maria: saw this spike during last few GPU backfills, started ~02:10 UTC. loss concentrated east-west between nodes in rack-b and rack-c.

tyler: can you paste the `ip link` / MTU for geneve and underlay? suspect MTU mismatch after recent node image rollout.

maria: paste: ``ip link show geneve0
4: geneve0: <BROADCAST,MULTICAST,UP,LOWER_UP> mtu 1450 qdisc noqueue state UNKNOWN mode DEFAULT group default qlen 1000
link/ether 6a:... brd ff:ff:ff:ff:ff:ff``
underlay eth0 mtu 9000 on both nodes.

raj: MTU 1450 on geneve is odd given 9000 underlay. Are we doing PMTU or rewrite? Could be fragmentation/encap offload got toggled.

sophie: we rolled kernel 6.3.x to rack-c yesterday with updated mlx5 firmware. There's a known offload regression that flips GSO/GRO behavior for VXLAN/Geneve in some drivers. :thinking:

maria: tcpdump snippet from node A -> node B during a spike: ``tcpdump -i geneve0 -nn -s 0 -w /tmp/geneve.pcap 'udp'`` shows repeated retransmits + small bursts of ICMP frag-needed from intermediate device.

tyler: can you try disabling encapsulation offloads temporarily? command: ``sudo ethtool -K geneve0 tx off rx off gso off gro off tso off`` and see if loss pattern stops.

maria: running now on node A. disabling offloads seemed to flatten the sawtooth for ~90s, then pattern reappeared on different node.

raj: that points to asymmetric egress path where some NICs/firmware handle offload differently. Also check `dmesg` for mlx5 warnings and `ethtool -k eth0` on the underlay.

sophie: opened INFRA-4321 to track kernel/firmware mismatch across racks. hypothesis: firmware 22.3 on rack-b vs 22.1 on rack-c causing different encapsulation handling.

maria: also correlating with K8s pod churn: recent GPU backfills cause live migrations (evictions) and we see packet loss spike within 30-60s after pod lands on destination.

tyler: does RDMA play here? we don't use RDMA for these training pods (TCP gRPC traffic), but check if mlx5 driver binds RDMA verbs which could impact offload.

raj: confirmed no ib0 on these nodes. RDMA stack not in use. driver still affects L2 offloads though.

maria: quick mitigation idea: force consistent geneve MTU to 1420 via CNI config and restart tunnel daemonset so all nodes converge, plus rollout firmware baseline.

sophie: agree. plan: 1) pin firmware on rack-b to 22.1 to match rack-c (ops will coordinate with hardware); 2) update CNI to set geneve mtu=1420 and deploy a rolling restart for tunnel pods; 3) add a short BPF-based drop-monitor to capture packets >1400 that get fragmented.

tyler: temporary policy: increase kube-svc affinity for GPU backfills to reduce cross-rack placement until firmware fix. low-friction and stops thrash.

maria: I'll run packet captures from both ends during next backfill and attach to INFRA-4321.

raj: I'll grep dmesg logs across racks for "mlx5" "err" "offload" and post findings.

sophie: I've scheduled firmware baseline job and will update infra runbook with offload-disable troubleshooting steps. assigning to infra team. :thumbsup:

maria: thanks — will update thread with pcap and any node-specific pattern. For now disabling offloads is a useful diagnostic but not a long-term fix.

netbot: NOTE: spike window 02:08-02:26 UTC, next autoscale expected 03:00 UTC.

maria: copying logs to /var/log/overlay-sawtooth/1832468101.tar.gz and linking to INFRA-4321.

sophie: fine-grain action items done. follow-ups: firmware baseline, CNI mtu change, backfill placement guard. good triage for now. :white_check_mark:
